correctness.rationale: The pumping argument forces every finite alphabet into one of the two 23-generator families. Each supplied 48-element integer-matrix list includes identity and all generators and is closed under right multiplication, hence bounds all word products by four. The 1024 ordered binary pairs are enumerated, with exact counts (216,28,2); unary and all three sharp witnesses are verified independently in Python using six-tuples and C++17 using full 3-by-3 matrices. Direct accepting-path enumeration also verifies witnesses. There is no infinite-word extrapolation from finite word length.

value.rationale: The 2026 singleton-SCC finite-ambiguity recurrence and 1991 known ternary lower bound leave the natural smallest unresolved n=3 interval 4 to 12. This theorem supplies the exact upper bound, the strict binary/ternary separation, and the complete two-maximal-type structural reduction, a useful first nontrivial exact benchmark. It does not claim a general n-state bound or an arbitrarily sliced recomputation.
